about: The external sources the validation report (docs/model/validation.md, #119) cites, and whether this environment fetched each one. Eleonora's ruling of 2 October 2026 (the claim wording, the fork, futures) and her scope of the same date (the Treasury clearing mandate). A source is marked fetched only if a session read the page itself; the rest are marked not fetched and are cited as she gave them. The page is rendered from this file by scripts/validation_report.py and is never edited by hand.

claim.sentence: To our knowledge, no public work forecasts the daily SOFR − IORB spread with strictly point-in-time public data and scores its exceedance probabilities with proper scoring rules against persistence baselines. Related efforts include Fed staff probability assessments for the fed funds − IOER spread (FOMC memo, 13 Sep 2019), a daily SOFR LSTM thesis scored by RMSE (Cornelissen, 2021), and futures-implied month-end premia, which tend to over-anticipate spikes (Gellert & Schlögl, 2021).
claim.ruling: Eleonora's ruling of 2 October 2026 on #119 and #120: this sentence, and no stronger form

sources.label: FOMC memo, 13 September 2019 (Fed staff, the fed funds − IOER spread)
Cornelissen (2021), the daily SOFR LSTM thesis
Gellert and Schlögl (2021), futures-implied month-end premia

fork.text: `nicholasberoud/repo-market-model` is a fork by Eleonora's collaborator, Nicholas Beroud. A reader who finds that repository with the same figures has found a copy of this project, not an independent replication.

futures.text: Futures are left out, both as a benchmark and as an input. CME futures data needs a licence and cannot be redistributed with this repository, and futures-implied month-end premia are documented to over-anticipate spikes (Gellert and Schlögl, 2021; CME's March 2019 example).
futures.ruling: Eleonora's ruling of 2 October 2026 on #119 and #120

clearing.scope: Eleonora's scope of 2 October 2026 on #119, relayed by the orchestrating session

speech.label: the New York Fed's speech of 9 July 2026
speech.says: requires eligible secondary-market Treasury cash transactions to be centrally cleared "by the end of 2026" and eligible Treasury repo and reverse repo "by mid-2027", and that repo activity "has begun migrating from uncleared to cleared markets"
speech.cleared_share: its footnote cites Office of Financial Research staff analysis that approximately 58 percent of repo volumes subject to the rule were already being cleared in the first eight months of 2025 (the scope of 2 October 2026 said early 2025)

methodology.label: the New York Fed's reference-rate methodology
methodology.says: SOFR includes the trades used in BGCR (tri-party and GCF repo) plus transactions cleared through FICC's delivery-versus-payment repo service, so it does not cover repo that is neither tri-party, GCF nor FICC-cleared

ofr_blog.label: the OFR's blog post of 22 April 2025
ofr_blog.says: the OFR expects little change to SOFR's median but fatter tails
